title: Model precision playbook and staged validation runway for catalog recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Ship a defensible per-model precision recommendation layer in the model catalog that pairs a small set of recommended profiles (FP8 / INT8 / FP16 fallback) with a staged calibration + validation runway. The playbook should provide automated checks (CI gating + runtime monitors), clear guardrails (accuracy thresholds, rollback triggers), and a lightweight set of artifacts (calibration vectors, sanity evals, fingerprint signatures) so SREs and PMs can safely enable lower-precision variants for production workloads.

Scope: Catalog-level metadata and automation for recommended precision profiles (not the core runtime kernels). Work covers: (1) profile spec and metadata schema, (2) offline calibration harness and sampling strategy, (3) validation metrics + thresholds, (4) rollout orchestration primitives for canary/shadow + auto-rollback, (5) CI gating and release checklist.

Success criteria: (a) For each curated model in the initial batch (gpt-3.5-style, Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B), produce a recommended profile that reduces token-cost by >=15% relative to FP16 for INT8/FP8 runs while keeping UX regressions below defined thresholds; (b) Deployed canary mechanism successfully detects accuracy regressions and rolls back within 10 minutes for 95% of simulated regressions; (c) All catalog recommendations include a human-readable rationale and a machine-readable fingerprint to tie calibration artifacts to a model version.

Proposed approach:
- Profile spec: define a compact profile JSON with attributes: precision, quant-scheme (symmetric/asymmetric), per-layer-exceptions, calibration-data-hash, validation-signature, expected-latency-gain, expected-cost-savings. Store profiles in model catalog metadata.
- Calibration harness: build levered pipeline that accepts model shard, representative prompt set, and outputs calibration tables + validation vectors. Harness will support two modes: deterministic offline (batch calibration for CI) and lightweight runtime warm-up sampling for production (shadow cache priming).
- Sampling strategy: dataset fingerprinting + shard-aware reservoir sampling. Create 3 canonical fingerprint buckets: conversational conversational-short, instruction-heavy, retrieval-augmented. Use per-bucket sampling quotas to avoid skew.
- Validation metrics: token-level LM perplexity delta, response-level embedding cosine similarity (average over 1k queries), semantic pass-rate on domain prompts (binary), and presence/ hallucination regressions flagged via heuristics. Define banded thresholds: green (<=1% perf delta and >=0.98 embedding cosine), yellow (1-3% delta or 0.95-0.98 cosine), red (>3% or <0.95). Profiles labeled with confidence band.
- Rollout: canary -> shadow -> gradual traffic ramp with automatic comparison against baseline model on the same requests. Rollback triggers: any metric moving into red for 5 consecutive minutes or a cumulative A/B failure rate >1% on critical prompts.
- CI gating: require calibration artifacts and validation report for any profile addition to catalog; PRs must include the dataset hash and a reproducible calibration script.

Trade-offs and decisions so far:
- FP8 offers larger memory and throughput wins but is brittle on certain attention-heavy layers. We will allow per-layer exceptions in the profile so the runtime can run sensitive layers at FP16 while the rest uses FP8. This hybrid approach is our preferred initial guardrail.
- Strong preference for conservative defaults for enterprise-critical models (customer_impact=high) — those will ship INT8 with higher confidence bands and explicit human approval.
- We will not attempt to fully automate quant scheme selection across all models on day 1; instead the first pass will target 12 curated models and expand once the runway matures.

Deliverables by milestone:
- M1 (2 weeks): profile schema + sample profiles for 6 models, acceptance criteria doc.
- M2 (6 weeks): offline calibration harness + CI integration, reproducible artifacts for curated models.
- M3 (10 weeks): rollout automation (shadow + canary) + Grafana dashboards and alerting rules.
- M4 (12 weeks): production-enablement checklist and documentation in Console to display recommended profile and rollback instructions.

Operational notes:
- Add a lightweight nightly job to recompute calibration signatures for modified model variants.
- Explicitly store calibration inputs (hashes only; raw datasets stored in secured drive) to allow reproducibility and auditing.
- Plan for a follow-up UX ticket to display per-profile risk indicators in the Console.

Risks:
- Calibration datasets may not represent customer traffic; mitigate by enabling runtime shadow sampling and providing per-customer opt-outs.
- False positives from heuristics causing unnecessary rollbacks; mitigate by requiring sustained deviation and multi-metric checks.

Open questions:
- What is the canonical set of domain buckets we should support beyond the initial three? (CC: PM/product to weigh in).
- Should we require manual sign-off for any profile that maps to a release with SLA-backed customers?

Overall this ticket integrates experimentation artifacts with production rollout primitives so catalog recommendations become actionable and reversible.

Action: add per-layer exclusion experiment for rotary embeddings.
